    require(
        isinstance(nodes, list)
        and 1 <= len(nodes) <= 500
        and all(isinstance(n, dict) for n in nodes),
        "source_invalid",
        "nodes",
        "Supply between one and 500 nodes.",
    )
    assert isinstance(nodes, list)
    require(
        not data.get("pinData") and not data.get("staticData"),
        "source_state_unsupported",
        "source_json",
        "Pinned or persistent source state needs explicit adaptation.",
    )
    settings = data.get("settings") or {}
    require(
        isinstance(settings, dict)
        and not (set(settings) - {"executionOrder"})
        and settings.get("executionOrder", "v1") == "v1",
        "source_settings_unsupported",
        "settings",
        "Source execution settings need adaptation.",
    )
    names: dict[str, int] = {}
    starts: list[int] = []
    for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
        path = f"nodes[{i}]"
        name = node.get("name")
        require(
            isinstance(name, str) and 0 < len(name) <= 200 and name not in names,
            "source_invalid",
            path,
            "Node names must be nonempty and unique.",
        )
        names[name] = i
        require(
            not node.get("credentials"),
            "credentials_require_mapping",
            path + ".credentials",
            "Source credentials require target connection mapping.",
            "Discover the live operation and permitted connection; do not copy credential IDs, names or tokens.",
        )
        unknown = set(node) - _UI_KEYS - set(_BEHAVIOR_DEFAULTS) - {"credentials"}
        require(
            not unknown and all(node.get(k, v) == v for k, v in _BEHAVIOR_DEFAULTS.items()),
            "node_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "A node execution option needs explicit adaptation.",
        )
        kind = str(node.get("type", ""))
        key = kind.removeprefix(_BASE) if kind.startswith(_BASE) else ""
        require(
            key in VERSIONS,
            "node_unsupported",
            path + ".type",
            "This node needs an adapter or a verified operation mapping.",
            "Discover native operations first, then assess HTTP or a reusable child workflow; an unrecognized node does not establish a missing extension.",
        )
        version = node.get("typeVersion")
        require(
            type(version) in {int, float} and version in VERSIONS[key],
            "node_version_unsupported",
            path + ".typeVersion",
            "This node version has not been qualified.",
        )
        require(
            isinstance(node.get("parameters", {}), dict),
            "source_invalid",
            path + ".parameters",
            "Node parameters must be an object.",
        )
        if key == "manualTrigger":
            starts.append(i)
    require(
        len(starts) == 1,
        "trigger_unsupported",
        "nodes",
        "Exactly one Manual Trigger is supported.",
        "Map webhook, schedule and app triggers explicitly; manual invocation does not preserve them.",
    )
    raw = data.get("connections", {})
    require(
        isinstance(raw, dict), "source_invalid", "connections", "Connections must be an object."
    )
    links: dict[int, list[int | None]] = {}
    parents: dict[int, int] = {}
    fanouts: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
    for name, channels in raw.items():
        require(
            name in names and isinstance(channels, dict),
            "graph_unsupported",
            "connections",
            "A source connection is invalid.",
        )
        require(
            not (set(channels) - {"main"}),
            "connection_kind_unsupported",
            "connections",
            "Non-main AI or auxiliary connections need semantic adaptation.",
        )
        outputs = channels.get("main", [])
        index = names[name]
        is_if = nodes[index]["type"] == _BASE + "if"
        require(
            isinstance(outputs, list) and len(outputs) <= (2 if is_if else 1),
            "graph_unsupported",
            "connections",
            "Unexpected output channels need adaptation.",
        )
        links[index] = []
        for targets in outputs:
            require(
                isinstance(targets, list),
                "graph_unsupported",
                "connections",
                "Output targets must be an array.",
            )
            require(
                len(targets) <= 1 or (parallel_fanout and not is_if),
                "fanout_unsupported",
                "connections",
                "Source fan-out needs explicit execution-order mapping.",
                "Map independent branches to native Group Parallel Run with parallel_fanout=true; source v1 sequential branch ordering must not be changed implicitly.",
            )
            translated = []
            for connection in targets:
                require(
                    isinstance(connection, dict)
                    and set(connection) <= {"node", "type", "index"}
                    and isinstance(connection.get("node"), str)
                    and connection["node"] in names
                    and connection.get("type") == "main"
                    and type(connection.get("index")) is int
                    and connection["index"] == 0,
                    "graph_unsupported",
                    "connections",
                    "An edge or target input needs explicit adaptation.",
                )
                target = names[connection["node"]]
                require(
                    target not in parents and target != starts[0],
                    "graph_unsupported",
                    "connections",
                    "Joins, repeated incoming edges or cycles need explicit adaptation.",
                )
                parents[target] = index
                translated.append(target)
            if len(translated) > 1:
                fanouts[index] = translated
                links[index].append(None)
            else:
                links[index].append(translated[0] if translated else None)
    order: list[int] = []
    queue = [starts[0]]
    while queue:
        index = queue.pop(0)
        require(
            index not in order,
            "graph_unsupported",
            "connections",
            "Cyclic control flow needs explicit adaptation.",
        )
        order.append(index)
        queue.extend(t for t in links.get(index, []) if t is not None)
        queue.extend(fanouts.get(index, []))
    require(
        len(order) == len(nodes),
        "graph_unsupported",
        "connections",
        "Disconnected nodes or cycles need explicit adaptation.",
    )
    return SourceGraph(nodes, order, links, parents, fanouts)

"""Qualified n8n HTTP Request translation and runtime object guard."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from .contracts import require
from .json_source import load_json
from .secrets import (
    _portable_reference,
    _sensitive_key,
)
from .target import edge, qualified_keys, step
from .values import CredentialInputs, literal_json, translate


def _parameters(
    raw: Any,
    incoming: str,
    path: str,
    credentials: CredentialInputs,
    *,
    headers: bool = False,
    body_values: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require(isinstance(raw, dict), "source_invalid", path, "Parameters must be an object.")
    qualified_keys(raw, {"parameters"}, path)
    rows = raw.get("parameters", [])
    require(isinstance(rows, list), "source_invalid", path, "Parameter entries must be an array.")
    result = {}
    names: set[str] = set()
    for row in rows:
        require(
            isinstance(row, dict)
            and set(row) <= {"name", "value"}
            and isinstance(row.get("name"), str)
            and row["name"],
            "source_invalid",
            path,
            "A parameter needs a static name and value.",
        )
        name = row["name"]
        key = name.lower() if headers else name
        authorization = key == "authorization" or (
            headers and key.replace("-", "_").endswith("_authorization")
        )
        require(
            key not in names and "={{" not in name and "{{" not in name,
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "Dynamic or repeated parameter names need adaptation.",
        )
        names.add(key)
        raw_value = row.get("value", "")
        if _sensitive_key(name) and not body_values:
            if isinstance(raw_value, str) and raw_value.startswith("="):
                translated = translate(raw_value, incoming, path, template=True)
                result[name] = (
                    translated
                    if _portable_reference(translated)
                    else credentials.reference(translated, authorization=authorization)
                )
            else:
                result[name] = credentials.reference(raw_value, authorization=authorization)
        else:
            result[name] = translate(raw_value, incoming, path, template=not body_values)
    return result


def http_step(
    node: dict[str, Any],
    index: int,
    incoming: str,
    credentials: CredentialInputs,
    *,
    object_response_nodes: list[int],
) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], str]:
    path = f"nodes[{index}].parameters"
    p = node.get("parameters", {})
    qualified_keys(
        p,
        {
            "method",
            "url",
            "authentication",
            "sendQuery",
            "queryParameters",
            "specifyQuery",
            "sendHeaders",
            "headerParameters",
            "specifyHeaders",
            "sendBody",
            "contentType",
            "specifyBody",
            "bodyParameters",
            "jsonBody",
            "options",
        },
        path,
        code="http_option_unsupported",
    )
    require(
        p.get("authentication", "none") == "none",
        "credentials_require_mapping",
        path,
        "HTTP authentication requires target mapping.",
    )
    options = p.get("options", {})
    require(isinstance(options, dict), "source_invalid", path, "HTTP options must be an object.")
    qualified_keys(options, {"timeout"}, path + ".options", code="http_option_unsupported")
    require(
        index in object_response_nodes,
        "http_object_contract_required",
        path,
        "n8n HTTP JSON arrays expand into items; an object response contract is required.",
        "Verify the provider returns one JSON object; otherwise build explicit For each/item mappings. Never assert this from a node name alone.",
    )
    method = p.get("method", "GET")
    require(
        isinstance(method, str)
        and method in {"GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"},
        "http_option_unsupported",
        path,
        "The HTTP method is not supported.",
    )
    raw_url = p.get("url")
    require(isinstance(raw_url, str), "source_invalid", path, "A URL is required.")
    # Expressions are translated before URL parsing, so unsupported JS is reported precisely.
    url_value = translate(raw_url, incoming, path + ".url", template=True)
    require(
        isinstance(url_value, str),
        "http_url_unsupported",
        path,
        "URL expressions must produce text.",
    )
    if url_value.startswith("{{ state.") and url_value.endswith(" }}"):
        url, query = url_value, {}
    else:
        url, query = credentials.url(url_value, path + ".url")
    for flag in ("sendQuery", "sendHeaders", "sendBody"):
        require(
            type(p.get(flag, False)) is bool,
            "source_invalid",
            path,
            "HTTP enable flags must be booleans.",
        )
    if p.get("sendQuery"):
        require(
            p.get("specifyQuery", "keypair") == "keypair",
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "This query encoding needs adaptation.",
        )
        explicit = _parameters(p.get("queryParameters", {}), incoming, path, credentials)
        require(
            not set(query).intersection(explicit),
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "Duplicate URL and explicit secret query fields need adaptation.",
        )
        query.update(explicit)
    else:
        require(
            not p.get("queryParameters"),
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "Inactive query settings need review.",
        )
    headers = {}
    if p.get("sendHeaders"):
        require(
            p.get("specifyHeaders", "keypair") == "keypair",
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "This header encoding needs adaptation.",
        )
        headers = _parameters(
            p.get("headerParameters", {}), incoming, path, credentials, headers=True
        )
    else:
        require(
            not p.get("headerParameters"),
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "Inactive headers need review.",
        )
    body = None
    if p.get("sendBody"):
        require(
            p.get("contentType", "json") == "json",
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "Only JSON request bodies are supported.",
        )
        if p.get("specifyBody", "keypair") == "json":
            raw = p.get("jsonBody")
            require(isinstance(raw, str), "source_invalid", path, "JSON body must be JSON text.")
            try:
                body = load_json(raw)
            except (ValueError, RecursionError):
                require(
                    False,
                    "expression_unsupported",
                    path,
                    "A JSON body expression needs adaptation.",
                )
            require(
                isinstance(body, (dict, list)),
                "http_option_unsupported",
                path,
                "Scalar JSON bodies need explicit target encoding.",
            )
            body = credentials.body(literal_json(body, path))
        else:
            require(
                p.get("specifyBody", "keypair") == "keypair",
                "http_option_unsupported",
                path,
                "This body encoding needs adaptation.",
            )
            body = credentials.body(
                _parameters(
                    p.get("bodyParameters", {}), incoming, path, credentials, body_values=True
                )
            )
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **headers}
    else:
        require(
            not p.get("bodyParameters") and not p.get("jsonBody"),
            "http_option_unsupported",
            path,
            "Inactive body settings need review.",
        )
    timeout = options.get("timeout", 300_000)
    require(
        type(timeout) in {int, float} and 0 < timeout <= 3_600_000,
        "http_option_unsupported",
        path,
        "A bounded HTTP timeout is required.",
    )
    base = f"n{index:04d}"
    target = f"state.n8n.{base}.response"
    config = {
        "method": method,
        "url": url,
        "headers": headers,
        "query_params": query,
        "auth_mode": "none",
        "auth_ref": "",
        "timeout_seconds": timeout / 1000,
        "expected_statuses": list(range(200, 300)),
        "response_mode": "inline",
        "response_target": target,
    }
    if body is not None:
        config["body_template"] = body
    request = step(base, "http_request", config)
    request["error_policy"] = {"on_error": "route_to_step"}
    # A violated object contract fails instead of silently treating an array as one item.
    shape = step(
        base + "_shape",
        "template",
        {
            "text": "{{ 'object' if response is mapping else 'invalid' }}",
            "format": "text",
            "inputs": [
                {
                    "name": "response",
                    "type": "json",
                    "required": True,
                    "source": target + ".response_body",
                }
            ],
            "result_target": f"state.n8n.{base}.shape",
        },
    )
    shape["error_policy"] = {"on_error": "route_to_step"}
    guard = step(
        base + "_object",
        "if",
        {
            "condition": {
                "selector": f"state.n8n.{base}.shape",
                "operator": "equals",
                "value": "object",
            }
        },
    )
    edges = [
        edge(base, "success", base + "_shape"),
        edge(base, "error", "failed"),
        edge(base + "_shape", "success", base + "_object"),
        edge(base + "_shape", "error", "failed"),
        edge(base + "_object", "false", "failed"),
    ]
    return [request, shape, guard], edges, target + ".response_body"

"""Deterministic, read-only n8n export to disabled v2 bundle conversion."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from itertools import pairwise
from typing import Any

import yaml

from .adapters import if_steps, set_steps
from .contracts import (
    ConversionBlocked,
    ConversionResult,
    require,
)
from .graph import parse_graph
from .http import http_step
from .parallel import (
    completion_edges,
    lane_http_steps,
    parallel_layout,
)
from .target import edge, step
from .values import CredentialInputs

SCHEMA_VERSION = "platform.workflow_bundle.v2"
BUNDLE_KIND = "workflow_bundle"


def convert_n8n(
    source_json: str,
    *,
    workflow_id: str,
    object_response_nodes: list[int] | None = None,
    parallel_fanout: bool = False,
) -> ConversionResult:
    """Convert a qualified subset, returning no bundle whenever semantics are unresolved.

    object_response_nodes uses zero-based source node indexes backed by an
    inspected provider response contract. It is not inferred from saved test data.
    Generated guards refuse a response outside that contract at runtime.
    """
    credentials = CredentialInputs()
    result: ConversionResult = {
        "status": "blocked",
        "source_format": "n8n.workflow.json",
        "bundle_yaml": None,
        "runtime_verified": False,
        "target_validation": "required",
        "issues": [],
        "node_mappings": [],
        "credential_inputs": [],
    }
    try:
        require(
            isinstance(workflow_id, str)
            and len(workflow_id) <= 120
            and re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*", workflow_id),
            "target_id_invalid",
            "workflow_id",
            "Use a stable lowercase workflow identifier.",
        )
        require(
            type(parallel_fanout) is bool,
            "parallel_mode_invalid",
            "parallel_fanout",
            "Parallel fan-out must be selected explicitly with a boolean.",
        )
        graph = parse_graph(source_json, parallel_fanout=parallel_fanout)
        layout = parallel_layout(graph)
        confirmed = object_response_nodes or []
        require(
            isinstance(confirmed, list)
            and all(
                type(i) is int
                and i in range(len(graph.nodes))
                and graph.nodes[i]["type"] == "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest"
                for i in confirmed
            ),
            "object_contract_invalid",
            "object_response_nodes",
            "Object-response indexes must name HTTP nodes in this export.",
        )
        steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        edges: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        items: dict[int, str] = {}
        ends: dict[int, str] = {}
        end_outcomes: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
        failures: list[ConversionBlocked] = []
        for index in graph.order:
            node = graph.nodes[index]
            base = f"n{index:04d}"
            kind = node["type"].removeprefix("n8n-nodes-base.")
            parent = graph.parents.get(index)
            incoming = items[parent] if parent is not None else "state.inputs"
            try:
                if kind == "httpRequest":
                    expanded, internal, item = http_step(
                        node, index, incoming, credentials, object_response_nodes=confirmed
                    )
                    if index in layout.membership:
                        expanded, internal = lane_http_steps(expanded)
                    edges.extend(internal)
                    outcomes = ["success"] if index in layout.membership else ["true"]
                elif kind == "set":
                    expanded, item = set_steps(node, index, incoming, credentials)
                    edges.extend(
                        edge(a["step_id"], "success", b["step_id"]) for a, b in pairwise(expanded)
                    )
                    outcomes = ["success"]
                elif kind == "if":
                    expanded, internal = if_steps(node, index, incoming)
                    edges.extend(internal)
                    item, outcomes = incoming, ["true", "false"]
                else:
                    require(
                        node.get("parameters", {}) == {},
                        "node_option_unsupported",
                        f"nodes[{index}].parameters",
                        "Trigger or No Op parameters need adaptation.",
                    )
                    item = f"state.n8n.{base}.item"
                    value = {} if kind == "manualTrigger" else {"source": incoming}
                    expanded, outcomes = (
                        [step(base, "set_variable", {"target": item, "value": value})],
                        ["success"],
                    )
                if index in layout.membership:
                    for member in expanded:
                        member.update(layout.membership[index])
                steps.extend(expanded)
                ends[index] = expanded[-1]["step_id"]
                items[index] = item
                end_outcomes[index] = outcomes
                result["node_mappings"].append(
                    {
                        "source_index": index,
                        "source_type": node["type"],
                        "target_step_ids": [s["step_id"] for s in expanded],
                        "status": "converted",
                    }
                )
            except ConversionBlocked as exc:
                if exc.issue["path"] == "parameters":
                    exc.issue["path"] = f"nodes[{index}].parameters"
                failures.append(exc)
                # Continue inspection using a non-emitted alias; no partial bundle is returned.
                items[index] = incoming
        if failures:
            result["issues"] = [f.issue for f in failures]
            return result
        edges.extend(completion_edges(graph, layout, ends, end_outcomes))
        steps.append(step("done", "stop_success", {"message": "Complete"}))
        if any(e["target"].get("id") == "failed" for e in edges):
            steps.append(
                step("failed", "stop_fail", {"message": "HTTP request or response contract failed"})
            )
        workflow = {
            "workflow_id": workflow_id,
            "display_name": workflow_id,
            "version": "0.1.0",
            "enabled": False,
            "trigger": {},
            "settings": {
                "callable": {
                    "enabled": True,
                    "input_mode": "fields",
                    "strict_inputs": True,
                    "trigger_channels": ["ui", "api", "mcp", "parent_workflow"],
                    "expected_inputs": credentials.fields,
                }
            },
            "participants": [],
            "tags": ["migration", "n8n"],
            "steps": steps,
            "groups": layout.groups,
            "execution_graph": {
                "schema_version": 1,
                "entry": {"kind": "step", "id": f"n{graph.order[0]:04d}"},
                "edges": edges,
            },
        }
        bundle = {
            "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
            "kind": BUNDLE_KIND,
            "metadata": {"source_format": "n8n.workflow.json"},
            "workflows": [workflow],
            "dependencies": {},
            "import_hints": {"default_enabled": False, "import_state": "draft"},
        }
        if layout.groups:
            result["issues"].append(
                {
                    "code": "n8n.parallel_fanout",
                    "path": "connections",
                    "message": "Independent source branches were explicitly adapted to native Parallel Run groups.",
                    "severity": "warning",
                    "blocking": False,
                    "repair_guidance": "Verify branch independence and source ordering/failure differences before live execution.",
                }
            )
        result["status"] = "converted"
        result["bundle_yaml"] = yaml.safe_dump(bundle, sort_keys=False)
        result["credential_inputs"] = credentials.fields
    except ConversionBlocked as exc:
        result["issues"].append(exc.issue)
    return result

# Publish a Flow Steward Workflow Template

The public catalog is <https://github.com/Flow-Steward/workflows>. Flow Steward
reads its `index.json` and lists the templates under **Workflows → Catalog**.
Each template is one exported YAML file in that repository. The catalog README
(`README.md`, section "Share a workflow") is the source of truth: read the
current copy before you start and follow it where it differs from this skill.

Publishing makes the workflow public. Get the user's explicit go-ahead before
opening the pull request.

What this needs, and what to do without it:

- **Flow Steward MCP** for the export. Without it, the user exports the file in
  the UI (step 2) and gives it to you.
- **GitHub**: your client's GitHub tools or an authenticated `gh` CLI, with the
  user's permission to act on their account. Without either, prepare the file,
  its catalog path and the pull request text, and tell the user to submit them
  in the browser (step 5). Do not claim that a pull request exists.
- **A terminal** only for the optional local catalog check; skip it and say so
  when there is none.

## 1. Prepare the workflow in Flow Steward

- **Name** (`display_name`): a readable title, not an identifier —
  "Import supplier stock from email attachments", not `stock_import`. At most
  120 characters.
- **Description**: at least 40 characters. Its first sentence becomes the card
  summary, so say what the workflow does.
- **Version**: semantic, such as `1.0.0` (the default for a new workflow). A
  version already published in the catalog for the same `workflow_id` is
  refused; raise it for every new submission. The workflow screens show no
  version field and the MCP tools do not change it; an administrator changes
  it through the workflow metadata API (read the workflow, then a full
  `PUT /api/workflows/<workflow_id>` with the same metadata and the new
  `version`; see the API reference). Tell the user when this step is needed.
  Confirm the new version in the exported file.
- It must be a current, phase-free workflow. A phase-based
  `platform.workflow_bundle.v1` export is refused.
- Validate it and run it at least once (a controlled Test Run, or a run through
  the `flow-steward-workflow-authoring` skill), so the template is known to
  work. Say in the pull request if it was not run.

## 2. Export

In the UI: **Workflows**, the workflow's **⋯** menu, then **Export YAML**. If
it calls other workflows, choose **Export YAML with child workflows**, so they
travel in the same file and the template installs complete. Through MCP:
`workflow_export(project_name, workflow_id, include_children=true)`.

One file is one template: the main workflow and the child workflows it calls,
nothing else. Do not hand-edit the exported file.

## 3. Privacy review

Exports leave configured secret values out, and the catalog check refuses a
value under keys such as `password`, `secret`, `api_key`, `access_token` or
`private_key`. That is not enough on its own. Read the whole file with the
user and look for:

- literal values in step settings and mappings: email addresses, customer or
  shop names, internal URLs and host names, file paths, account ids;
- prompts and notes that quote real data;
- sample data embedded in inputs.

If something private is there, change it in Flow Steward (use a placeholder or
an input) and export again, rather than editing the file.

## 4. Add the file to the catalog

1. Fork `Flow-Steward/workflows` and create a branch.
2. Pick one category folder from the repository's `categories.json` (for
   example `ai`, `crm`, `ecommerce`, `email`, `marketing`, `operations`,
   `other`). The category is the author's choice; reviewers only check that it
   is in the list.

Optionally run the check locally from the catalog clone (it uses a Python

pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/build_index.py --check --base origin/main

## 5. Open the pull request

Title: "Add <workflow title> <version>". In the description say what the

name: flow-steward-report-issue
description: Use when a Flow Steward user wants to report a bug, a crash, a wrong result or a confusing behavior, or to request a feature, on GitHub Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app; collects the System Diagnostics report and the facts maintainers need.
---

# Report a Flow Steward Bug or Request a Feature

Issues and feature requests go to
<https://github.com/Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app/issues>. Help the user write
one report that a maintainer can act on without a follow-up question. Work with
the user: you collect and draft, the user confirms what is sent.

This skill reports a problem; it does not fix it. Do not change Flow Steward
code, settings or data while preparing a report. A workaround the user can
apply in their own workflow is worth noting in the issue.

What this needs, and what to do without it:

- **GitHub**: your client's GitHub tools or an authenticated `gh` CLI, and the
  user's permission to post on their behalf. Without them, produce the finished
  draft and the link from step 6; the user submits it in the browser. Never
  claim that an issue was filed when it was not.
- **The diagnostics report** comes from the user or their administrator
  (step 2). You do not need a terminal or server access for it.

**Security vulnerabilities are never public issues.** If the problem lets
someone read, change or run something they should not, stop and tell the user
to email `security@flow-steward.org` with the subject prefix `[SECURITY]`, as
`SECURITY.md` in the repository says. Do not file it on GitHub.

## 1. Search first

Search existing issues, open and closed, with two or three key words from the
error message or the feature:

```bash
gh issue list --repo Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app --state all --search "<words>"
```

Without `gh`, open
`https://github.com/Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app/issues?q=<words>`. If an
issue already describes the problem, offer to add a comment with the new facts
(version, diagnostics, steps) instead of opening a duplicate.

## 2. Get the System Diagnostics report

Every bug report needs the diagnostics JSON. It says how the installation is
built and how it runs: the Flow Steward version and image identity, Compact or
Scalable, CPU architecture and resources, database and broker versions, each
service and its health, the installed extensions with their version and state,
and which settings are customised. It has **no logs, no job content and no
setting values** beyond a short list of deployment-shape settings (such as the
profile, storage backend and log level); every configured secret value is
removed wherever it appears.

Ask the user to get it one of two ways:

- **In the UI** (administrator only): **System → Monitoring**, then
  **Download diagnostics**. The file is
  `flow-steward-diagnostics-<UTC stamp>.json`. This is the usual way.
- **From the command line**, by someone with access to the server, in the
  installation folder:

  ```bash
  ./flow-steward reports diagnostics
  ```

  It also collects host facts and the `doctor` result, writes
  `.flow-steward/diagnostics/flow-steward-diagnostics-<UTC stamp>.json` and
  prints the path.

Administrators can also fetch it from the API with
`GET /api/system/diagnostics/report`; an agent does that only when the user
already gave it that access for this purpose. The command-line report is the most
complete, because only the host sees Docker and the containers; prefer it when
the user has access to the server. A non-administrator cannot download the
report; ask the user to get it from their administrator. If the stack is down so badly that neither works, say so in the
issue and include the output of `./flow-steward status` and
`./flow-steward doctor` instead.

Even though the report is redacted, **tell the user to open the file and glance
through it before attaching it**: host names, extension ids and customised
setting names may still be things they prefer not to publish. Never edit the
report to hide a problem; leave out a whole section only if the user insists,
and say in the issue that it was trimmed.

## 3. Collect the facts

- **Version**: from the diagnostics file, or `./flow-steward release info`.
- **What happened**: the exact error text, copied, not paraphrased.
- **Steps to reproduce**: numbered, starting from a known state (which page,
  which workflow or extension, what input). Ask the user to repeat them once
  to confirm the problem still happens.
- **Expected and actual result**: one sentence each.
- **Job**: the job id, the workflow id and the failing step name when a run
  failed. Do not paste the job's data.
- **Screenshots**: of the error or the wrong screen, after cropping out
  customer data, tokens and email addresses.
- **Since when**: did it work before (which version), and what changed (an
  update, a new extension, a setting).

A job page also has **Download full report**. Secrets are redacted in it, but
it contains the job's messages, logs, events and step data, which is often
customer data. Do not attach it to a public issue. Mention that it exists and
offer it privately if a maintainer asks.

## 4. Never publish

Passwords, API keys, tokens, cookies, `.env` contents, connection strings,
private keys, setup links, customer names, emails, orders or file contents.
Check everything you paste — log excerpts and screenshots included. Replace a
value with `<redacted>` when the shape matters.

## 5. Draft the issue

Title: what is wrong, where, in plain words, for example
"Workflow import fails when a child workflow uses a Wait step".

```markdown
## What happened
<exact error text and where it appears>

## Steps to reproduce
1. ...

## Expected
...

## Actual
...

## Environment
- Flow Steward version: <x.y.z>
- Profile: Compact | Scalable
- Job id / workflow id: <if any>
- System Diagnostics report: attached (`flow-steward-diagnostics-<stamp>.json`)

## Notes
<since when, what changed, workaround if any>
```

For a feature request, replace the middle sections with: the problem the user
has today, what they would like to do instead, and how they work around it
now. Diagnostics are optional for a feature request.

Show the draft to the user and get an explicit yes before sending it.

## 6. File it

With an authenticated `gh` (`gh auth status`):

```bash
gh issue create --repo Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app --title "<title>" --body-file issue.md
```

`gh issue create` cannot attach files. After creating the issue, give the user
its URL and ask them to drag the diagnostics JSON (and screenshots) into a
comment in the browser. GitHub accepts `.json` attachments; if their browser
refuses, they can zip the file first.

Without `gh`, open
`https://github.com/Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app/issues/new/choose` and pick
**Bug report** (or **Feature request**). The bug form has a required System
Diagnostics field: the user drags the JSON there. Copy each section of the
draft into its field, attach screenshots, and let the user do the final click.

Report the issue URL back. Do not open more than one issue for one problem.

# Flow Steward Automations

You work through the user's configured, authenticated Flow Steward MCP
connection. Everything you need for ordinary work is in this skill, its
`references/` files and the live MCP contracts; no checkout, terminal or
documentation search is required.

- The server owns permissions, contracts and runtime behavior. `tools/list`
  shows the tools this token may call and their current arguments; the schema
  tools (`workflow_authoring_schema`, `agent_authoring_schema`,
  `skill_authoring_schema`) return the current request bodies. Read them
  instead of guessing fields.
- A missing tool means this token lacks the scope or the server lacks the
  operation. Say which operation is unavailable; never ask for another token,
  change credentials, install a server or reach the API another way.
- Failures stay failures. A refused read is not an empty result; a refused
  write did not happen.

## Limits you state instead of working around

| Missing | What to say and do |
| --- | --- |
| No Flow Steward MCP in this client | You cannot read or change anything in Flow Steward. Ask the user to connect the MCP server as their installation's AI-agent setup describes, then continue. |
| Write tools absent from `tools/list` | Creating, changing and enabling agents, skills and workflows needs an administrator user and a token with `admin:all`. Report it; continue with what the token can read. |
| An integration the automation needs | See "Missing integrations" below. A skill is never a substitute. |
| A platform defect | Collect the facts and use the `flow-steward-report-issue` skill. Changing Flow Steward code is not a fix you offer; a workaround inside the automation is. |
| GitHub access | Only issue reports and catalog publishing need it; those skills say what to do without it. |

Never enable, run, approve, cancel, restart, publish or install anything the
user did not ask for. Asking to build an automation is not asking to run it.

## Build an automation

Agree on the outcome first: trigger, inputs, outputs, which systems it reads
or changes, and who approves what. Then work in this order.

### 1. Discover what exists

1. `project_list`; keep the exact `project_name` the tools take.
2. `workflow_examples_search(project_name, query)`: a workflow that already
   does the job is reused, not duplicated. Inspect candidates with
   `capability_describe(project_name, "workflow:<id>")` or
   `workflow_definition(workflow_id)`.
3. `capability_search(project_name, query, kinds)` for tools, agents, skills
   and workflows; `capability_describe` for one component's live operation
   contract and, for a tool, its required connection types and the project's
   connections with their readiness and `setup_url`. Pick an `operation_id`
   for multi-operation tools. Report knowledge freshness when it is returned.
4. `agent_list(search)` and `skill_list(search)` list registry objects,
   disabled ones included; `capability_search` hides disabled objects. Reuse
   a fitting agent or skill instead of creating a near-duplicate.
5. `model_options` lists the providers and models the account may select.
   Leave `config.provider`/`config.model` empty to inherit the project route
   unless the user asked for a specific model.

### 2. Missing integrations

An external system (a shop, a mailbox, a CRM, a file store) is reached through
a tool that an installed extension provides and a ready project connection.

- No matching tool: the integration is missing. Say which system and which
  operation are needed, and that an administrator installs the extension
  (Extensions → Catalog in the UI) and creates its connection. Do not install
  anything, and do not promise that such an extension exists.
- A tool exists but no connection is ready: give the returned `setup_url` and
  what readiness reported. The user sets up the connection; you never handle
  its secrets.
- Never write a skill or an agent prompt that claims to call a system no tool
  reaches. A skill is instructions for an agent; it does not create an
  integration. Never put credentials, tokens or private URLs into a skill,
  prompt, bundle or input.

Stop at the blocker, show what is ready and what is missing, and continue
only with the user's decision.

### 3. Create skills and agents

Only when nothing existing fits. Fields, enablement and the conflict
procedure are in [references/agents-and-skills.md](references/agents-and-skills.md).

1. `skill_authoring_schema`, then `skill_create(skill)` with a stable
   `skill_id` and a readable `display_name`; it is saved disabled.
   `skill_inputs_set`/`skill_outputs_set` replace its whole contract lists;
   `skill_validate` reports readiness.
2. `agent_authoring_schema`, then `agent_create(agent)`; it is saved disabled.
   Assign skills with `agent_skill_assign(agent_id, skill_id, skill_prompt)`;
   `agent_skill_set_instructions` replaces one assignment's instructions.
   `agent_validate` reports readiness.
3. Only enabled objects can be wired together: `agent_skill_assign` refuses a
   disabled skill (`skill.disabled`), and a workflow draft that names a
   disabled agent is refused with `authoring.reference_not_permitted`. When
   the user asked you to build the automation, enable each new skill
   (`skill_validate`, then `skill_set_enabled(skill_id, true)`) before you
   assign it, and each new agent (`agent_validate`, then
   `agent_set_enabled(agent_id, true)`) before you compose the workflow, and
   tell the user which ones you enabled. The workflow itself is still saved
   disabled.
4. A `registry_id_conflict` or `registry_name_conflict` changes nothing:
   follow the conflict procedure in the reference. Never rename or overwrite
   on your own.

A valid readiness result is a static check; it does not prove that a run
works.

### 4. Compose the workflow

1. `workflow_authoring_schema(step_kind)` returns the current bundle sample
   (`minimal_bundle_yaml`) and persisted step fields. Start from it or from a
   permitted export.
2. Author exactly one workflow in `platform.workflow_bundle.v2` with an
   explicit stable `workflow_id` and a readable `display_name`: its `steps` (a
   step in a loop or parallel group names its `group_id`, in a lanes body its
   `lane_id`), its `groups`, and one `execution_graph` with an `entry` and
   edges `source → outcome → target`. There are no phases. Route every outcome
   (`success`, `true`/`false`, each switch `case_id` plus `default`,
   `approved`/`rejected`) to exactly one target; end root paths at
   `stop_success` or `stop_fail`. A phase-based v1 bundle is refused, not
   converted.
3. Reference agents, skills, tools and child workflows by the exact ids you
   discovered or created. Only `use_existing`/`map_existing` resolutions are
   supported.

### 5. Validate: validation is not execution

`workflow_draft_validate(project_name, bundle_yaml, resolutions)` writes
nothing. Repair real structural, reference, mapping and contract issues and
validate again, keeping the same id. Read `can_save`, the issues and the
performed and unperformed checks. Tell the user plainly that validation does
not run the workflow, call providers or prove that external systems accept the
data. Missing dependencies are reported as such, never replaced with
placeholders.

### 6. Save a disabled draft

When the user wants it created and validation allows it, call
`workflow_draft_save` with the same bundle and resolutions. It creates one
disabled workflow and never overwrites one. Report the saved id,
`enabled=false`, the returned `editor_url` and the remaining issues, exactly as
returned. A timeout or unclear answer is handled under "Uncertain results".

### 7. Enable only on request

Enabling is a separate decision. When the user asks for it:

1. `workflow_definition(workflow_id)` for the current `revision`, then
   `workflow_set_enabled(workflow_id, true, expected_revision)`. A 400 lists
   the readiness issues; a 409 means the workflow changed, so read it again.
2. If readiness names a disabled agent or skill the workflow uses, enable it
   (`skill_set_enabled(skill_id, true)` before `agent_set_enabled(agent_id,
   true)`) and try again. Each is refused with its own readiness issues when
   it is not ready.

Enabling does not run anything.

### 8. Run and read the result

Only when the user asks to run it.

1. `workflow_contract(workflow_id, project_name)` gives the inputs. Ask for
   every missing required input; do not invent values.
2. `workflow_trigger(project_name, workflow_id, payload, files=...)`. File
   inputs carry `input_name`, `filename`, `mime_type` and `content_base64`,
   never server paths or URLs. `test_mode=true` asks extensions to suppress
   the external effects they declare as suppressible; it does not guarantee
   that nothing outside changes, so say so before a test run that touches
   real systems. The workflow must be enabled.
3. Follow the returned `job_id` with `job_status`; read `job_result` for the
   outcome and `job_errors`/`job_incident` on failure. Judge the outcome by the
   job's status, not by a generic completion flag. A pending approval waits for
   the human: see [references/runs-approvals-reports.md](references/runs-approvals-reports.md).

Report what actually ran: job id, status, outputs or errors, and what was not
verified.

## Change an existing workflow

`workflow_draft_save` never edits an existing workflow.

1. `workflow_definition(workflow_id)` (disabled workflows included): steps,
   groups, execution graph and `revision`.
2. `workflow_apply_changes(workflow_id, expected_revision, operations,
   dry_run=true)` with one atomic set of `create_step`, `create_group`,
   `update_step_config`, `change_step_kind`, `update_group_config`,
   `set_entry`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `insert_step_between`, `move_step`,
   `delete_step` and `delete_group`, using stable ids so later operations can
   name new nodes. The dry run shows the resulting issues and which of them
   would refuse the set.
3. Apply the same set without `dry_run`. It becomes one new revision or
   nothing is saved. `workflow_revision_conflict` (409) means someone changed
   the workflow: read the definition again and rebuild the set; never resend a
   stale set.
4. A moved step loses its edges and a deleted step leaves no bypass: reconnect
   in the same set. An enabled workflow refuses a result with blocking issues
   and keeps running its current revision; do not disable it to force a
   change unless the user asked. `workflow.change.reference_unavailable` means
   a named agent, child workflow, connection or install is not usable by the
   workflow's account; it does not say whether a foreign id exists.

Related changes:

- `workflow_convert_group` moves a group into a new child workflow. It
  previews by default; apply only with the current `preview_digest` and
  revision.
- Hooks: `workflow_hooks_list` and `workflow_hook_get` read a workflow's hooks
  and bindings; `workflow_hook_preview` runs every binding check without
  saving; `workflow_hook_bind`/`workflow_hook_unbind` save the next binding
  revision at `expected_revision`; `workflow_hook_create_and_bind` creates the
  empty workflow that holds a hook's steps.
- Before changing a workflow's inputs or outputs, `workflow_where_used` lists
  the Invoke steps and hook bindings that call it.

Agents and skills have no revision: the last write wins. Read the object right
before `agent_update`/`skill_update` and send only the fields you change.

## Read and repair disabled objects

- List them: `workflow_list(project_name, enabled_only=false,
  include_validation=true)`, `agent_list`, `skill_list` (disabled included by
  default).
- Find out why they are not ready: `workflow_validate(workflow_id,
  project_name)` and `workflow_suggestions` for a workflow, `agent_validate`,
  `skill_validate`.
- `workflow_definition`, `agent_get` and `skill_get` read disabled objects.
  Discovery tools (`capability_search`, `capability_describe`) may not show
  them; that is not proof that they do not exist.
- Repair with the change tools, validate again, and enable only when the user
  asks. Disabling is refused while enabled workflows depend on the object; the
  error names them.

## Uncertain results

A timeout, dropped connection or unreadable answer after a write means the
outcome is unknown.

- Read before retrying: `workflow_definition`/`workflow_list` for a
  workflow, `agent_get`/`skill_get` for registry objects.
- Retry a draft save only with the same id and an unchanged bundle. A
  `workflow_id_conflict` or a name conflict after an uncertain save may be your
  own earlier call: compare what you read with what you sent. If it matches,
  say that its origin is unconfirmed (you cannot prove that your call created
  it) and continue with it. If it differs, treat it as someone else's object.
- Seeing an object proves that it exists, not who created it or that its
  content matches. Only a confirmed result supports "created".
- Never switch to a new id automatically to get past a conflict. A new id is
  used only when the user asks for an additional object.

## Export and import

`workflow_export(project_name, workflow_id, include_children)` returns a
`platform.workflow_bundle.v2` YAML (`bundle_yaml`); use `include_children=true`
when it calls other workflows. `workflow_import(project_name, bundle_yaml,
target_workflow_id, resolutions)` creates disabled drafts and needs draft-save
authority. Exports omit secret values; still read one before it leaves the
installation. To share a workflow in the public catalog, use the
`flow-steward-publish-workflow` skill.

## Operational questions

Runs, failures, stuck jobs, approvals, cancel and restart, and reports:
[references/runs-approvals-reports.md](references/runs-approvals-reports.md).

# Agents and Skills

Agents and skills are account registry objects. Every tool here needs an
administrator user, and a token needs `admin:all`, reads included. The schema
tools return the current bodies; read them before the first write in a
conversation instead of relying on remembered fields.

## Skills

- `skill_authoring_schema`: `create.json_schema` is the body of
  `skill_create`, `patch.json_schema` the `changes` of `skill_update`, and
  `related.inputs`/`related.outputs` the item schema of the contract lists.
- `skill_create(skill)` creates exactly `skill['skill_id']`, saved disabled.
  Omitted fields take schema defaults. The result has `status`, `skill_id` and
  the readiness `validation`.
- `skill_update(skill_id, changes)`: every field sent replaces the stored
  value; null never clears one; an empty `changes` answers `no_change`.
- `skill_inputs_set`/`skill_outputs_set` replace the whole list (items: name,
  type, description, required). Invalid items are refused and nothing changes.
  Agents using the skill pick up the new contract, so check
  `agent_list`/`agent_get` for its users before changing it.
- `skill_validate` checks readiness without changing anything;
  `skill_set_enabled(skill_id, enabled)` sets exactly that state. Disabling is
  refused while enabled workflows depend on an agent using the skill.

A skill is instructions for an agent. It does not reach any external system,
and it holds no credentials.

## Agents

- `agent_authoring_schema`: `create.json_schema` is the body of `agent_create`,
  `patch.json_schema` the `changes` of `agent_update`, `patch.semantics` how a
  patch merges, `related` the readiness, enable and assignment operations.
- `agent_create(agent)` creates exactly `agent['agent_id']`, saved disabled.
  Assign skills afterwards with `agent_skill_assign`: a `skills` list in the
  create body stores the assignment without its `skill_prompt` and does not
  refuse a disabled skill.
- `agent_update(agent_id, changes)`: only the fields sent change; null never
  clears; `config` and `prompts` merge shallowly; an empty
  `config.provider`/`config.model` inherits the project route. Skills and
  tools are refused here.
- `agent_skill_assign(agent_id, skill_id, skill_prompt)` adds a skill with
  agent-specific instructions; an already assigned skill is a 409, an unknown
  one a 404, a disabled one (`skill.disabled`) or one the agent's contract
  cannot use is refused with its issues. Enable a new skill before assigning
  it.
  `agent_skill_unassign` removes it; `agent_skill_set_instructions` replaces
  the instructions of one assignment.
- `agent_validate` checks readiness; `agent_set_enabled(agent_id, enabled)`
  sets exactly that state. Enabling needs a valid readiness result; disabling
  is refused while enabled workflows run the agent.
- `model_options` gives the selectable `provider_id`/`model_id` values.

Not available through MCP: reordering skills, replacing all relationships at
once, an agent's tools, full replacement, clone, history, restore and delete.
Say so and point the user to the registry screens when they need one.

## Read before you write: the last write wins

Agents and skills have no revision check. Another person or agent may change
the same object between your read and your write, and your write replaces what
it names.

- Read with `agent_get`/`skill_get` right before each change, and send only
  the fields you mean to change.
- If the read shows changes you did not expect, show them to the user before
  writing.
- After an uncertain result, read again before any retry.

## Conflicts

A refused write is a tool error whose `error.details` carries the route's
payload unchanged. Nothing was saved and nothing is renamed or retried for you.

### `registry_id_conflict`

The id is taken. The taken object may be invisible to this user (in the Trash
or another account), so the payload may show no match. `suggested_id` is a free
id at the time of the answer; nothing reserves it.

- After an uncertain create of that same id: read it with `agent_get` or
  `skill_get`. If you can read it and it matches what you sent, it is probably
  your own object: say that its origin is unconfirmed and continue with it. If
  you cannot read it, or it differs, it is not yours.
- Otherwise tell the user the id is taken and offer the suggested id or one
  they choose. Create under a new id only with their answer.

### `registry_name_conflict`

The display name is used by objects this user can see. The payload has
`matches` (each with `id`, `display_name`, `enabled`, `updated_at`, `origin`,
and `used_by` with the workflows or agents that use it), truncation flags when
there are more, and `suggested_display_name`, a hint nothing reserves.

1. Read each match (`agent_get`/`skill_get`).
2. If a match is the object you just tried to create after an uncertain
   result (same id, same content), say that its origin is unconfirmed and
   continue with it. Do not create another one.
3. Otherwise show the user every match: id, enabled state, last change,
   origin, where it is used (say when the list is truncated) and how it differs
   from what you meant to create. Ask whether to reuse or change the existing
   object, or which new name to use. Wait for the answer.

Changing an existing object that other workflows use changes them too; say
which ones before you write.

### Other refusals

- `Contract validation failed` (400) carries `issues`: fix them and try again.
- A dependency conflict (409) names the enabled workflows that depend on the
  object; disabling waits until they no longer do, which is the user's call.

# Runs, Approvals and Reports

Answer operational questions with the job and report tools. Resolve names
through `project_list` and `workflow_list`, and keep the exact ids the tools
return. An omitted filter means the caller's whole scope: never drop a filter
the user asked for, and never widen a query because a narrow one failed.

## Find runs

- `job_list(project_id, workflow_id, status, search, page, per_page)` lists
  runs within the caller's scope. `status` takes one status or a comma list.
  Prefer it to `project_jobs` for anything beyond a glance at recent runs.
- `job_list(..., group_by="attention")` groups runs for triage (failed,
  stuck, waiting). Treat it as a snapshot unless the response says it is
  complete.
- Read the paging and truncation fields every response returns. Follow the
  pages to the end before you state a total, and say so when the answer covers
  only part of the runs or when the inventory changed while you read it.
- `job_list` has no date filter. For a period, filter the returned timestamps
  yourself and say which timestamp (queued, started or finished) you used.

## Inspect one run

- `job_status` for a bounded current summary; `job_result` for the final or
  partial result bundle. Judge success by the job's status, not by a generic
  completion flag, and note when messages or logs in the bundle are cut.
- `workflow_run_report(job_id, wait_seconds)` shows the report a workflow
  returns (its Interface report output) to the user in the host's report
  viewer. You receive only its title, summary text and counts, never its rows.
  `wait_seconds` (0-30) waits for a running job; state `pending` means call
  again, `no_report` means the run returned none.
- On failure: `job_errors`, `job_incident`, `job_trace`; for detail,
  `job_messages`, `job_logs`, `job_events` with their cursors;
  `job_runtime_journal` and `job_decision_overrides` when the question is about
  routing decisions; `job_usage_breakdown` for token usage.
- `workflow_stats(project_name, workflow_id)` for a workflow's run statistics.

Present job ids, the observed status, the error or gate and the next useful
action. Separate a run that is still going from a finished one.

## Approvals

- `job_approvals_pending` lists runs waiting for a human decision in the
  caller's scope; narrow it to the requested project or workflow yourself.
  `job_approval(job_id)` shows the active gate, `job_approvals(job_id)` its
  history.
- `awaiting_timer` (a Wait step) and `awaiting_child` (a parent waiting for a
  child workflow) are not approvals. A parent's pending decision lives on the
  child job it links to.
- Decide only with the human's actual decision:
  `job_approval_decide(thread_id, approval_id, approved, idempotency_key,
  comment, action)` with the gate's own `thread_id` and `approval_id` and a
  stable `idempotency_key` reused on retry. Read `allowed_actions`; an
  exhausted rework budget offers only `approve` and `abort`. Permission to
  start a run is never permission to approve it.

## Cancel, restart, acknowledge

Only when the user asks, and after `job_status` shows the run's state:

- `job_cancel(job_id, comment)` for a pending or running job.
- `job_restart(job_id)` re-runs a failed or cancelled job with the same
  inputs. Never restart a run that is still active or waiting (timer, child,
  approval): it would start a duplicate. If the tool refuses, report its
  reason.
- `job_acknowledge`/`job_unacknowledge` mark triage state; they do not fix
  anything.

## Reports

`report_generate(report_type, params, persist)`:

- Operational types `activity_daily`, `project_summary`, `project_stats` take
  `params.project_id`, an exact `params.workflow_id`, and either
  `params.range` (default `7d`) or ISO `params.start_date`/`params.end_date`.
  Job types `job_summary` and `job_usage_breakdown` need `params.job_id`.
- `range="7d"` is a rolling 168-hour UTC window. Explicit dates are inclusive
  UTC calendar days. For a local "today", convert the user's local day to UTC
  boundaries; UTC-day aggregates cannot prove a local-day total, so label them
  UTC or use complete job pages filtered by timestamp.
- `persist=false` skips storing the report but still needs report write
  permission. `report_get(report_id)` reads a stored report.
- These reports describe activity and token usage. Use provider billing or
  your own external analysis for financial totals.

Return the actual window, filters, coverage, report id when stored, and the
limitations together with the results.

## Notifications

`project_notification_routes` and `project_notification_deliveries` show where
a project's notifications go and whether they were delivered.
`dispatch_project_notification` sends one; it reaches real recipients, so use it
only when the user asks.

# Flow Steward Developer

Agent skills for developers who build Flow Steward extensions or change the
core repository. They work from a terminal with the existing Flow Steward CLI,
the extension SDK, Git and Docker. They need no Flow Steward MCP connection and
no token.

| Skill | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `flow-steward-extension-authoring` | Build or change an extension against the target release's manifest, SDK and CLI lifecycle, and validate and test it. |
| `flow-steward-publish-extension` | Release an extension, and later versions, and list it in the public catalog `Flow-Steward/extensions`. |
| `flow-steward-contribute-code` | Fix a bug or propose an improvement in `Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app`, from the issue to a reviewed pull request. |
| `flow-steward-report-issue` | Report a bug or request a feature on GitHub with the System Diagnostics report. |

Building and running automations through MCP is in the separate
**Flow Steward Operator** package (`flow-steward-operator`). Install either
package or both; neither needs the other.

## Before you start

- A client that can run terminal commands and edit files.
- Git, Docker with Compose v2, and a Flow Steward application checkout
  installed in the Development environment for validation and tests.
- GitHub access through your client's own GitHub tools or the `gh` CLI for
  forks, releases and pull requests.

When one of them is missing, the skills say which step it blocks instead of
working around it. This package contains no address, token or server
configuration.

## Install

The directory containing this README is the plugin root: `plugin.json`
(Agent Plugins 1.0.0, also read by the OpenAI plugin directory),
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, the package icon
and `skills/`. Install that directory, not only `.claude-plugin/` and not the
whole application repository. Review the files first and keep a copy of the
version you replace.

Each Flow Steward release on GitHub also carries this package as
`flow-steward-developer-<version>.zip` and `.tar.gz`, with the plugin root at
the archive root, and a marketplace archive with both packages,
`flow-steward-agent-skills-<Core version>.zip`. Check a download against the
release's `SHA256SUMS`. Which clients support which setup is listed in the
[compatibility matrix](https://github.com/Flow-Steward/flow-steward-app/blob/main/docs/agent-skills/COMPATIBILITY.md).

The next example uses a local marketplace folder of your choice that holds this
directory at `plugins/flow-steward-developer`.

### Codex

Create or extend `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` in the marketplace folder;
keep other entries:

```json
{
  "name": "flow-steward-local",
  "plugins": [{
    "name": "flow-steward-developer",
    "source": {"source": "local", "path": "./plugins/flow-steward-developer"},
    "policy": {"installation": "AVAILABLE", "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"},
    "category": "Productivity"
  }]
}
```

From the marketplace folder, check your CLI's help, then register it:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add .
```

The CLI has no install command: in an interactive session open `/plugins`,
choose the `flow-steward-local` marketplace and install `flow-steward-developer`,
or install it from the Plugins tab of the ChatGPT desktop app. Start a new
session and find the four skills in its skills listing. To update, replace
the plugin directory, run
`codex plugin marketplace upgrade flow-steward-local`; the client runs a cached
copy, so compare the installed files with the new ones before relying on the
update, and start a new session. To remove the plugin, uninstall it in
`/plugins` or the app's Plugins tab, or run
`codex plugin marketplace remove flow-steward-local` to drop the whole local
marketplace. See [Package your plugin](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins)
and [Plugins](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins).

### Cursor

Copy this directory to `~/.cursor/plugins/local/flow-steward-developer`, reload
the window and find the skills under Customize. Your organization must allow
local plugin imports. Cursor reads `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`. To update,
replace the directory and reload; to remove, delete it and reload. See
[Cursor plugins](https://cursor.com/docs/plugins).

### Claude Code

The application repository's `docs/agent-skills` folder, and the
`flow-steward-agent-skills` folder inside the release's marketplace archive,
are a ready local marketplace named `flow-steward` that lists both packages:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add /absolute/path/to/flow-steward-agent-skills
claude plugin install flow-steward-developer@flow-steward
claude plugin details flow-steward-developer@flow-steward
```

`details` lists the four skills. In a session they appear as
`/flow-steward-developer:flow-steward-extension-authoring` and so on. For one
session without installing, start the client with
`claude --plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/flow-steward-developer`; the option also
takes the release's `flow-steward-developer-<version>.zip`.

To update, put the new release's marketplace folder in place of the old one
(each release raises `version`), run `claude plugin marketplace update flow-steward`
and `claude plugin update flow-steward-developer@flow-steward`, and
restart. To remove: `claude plugin uninstall flow-steward-developer@flow-steward`,
then `claude plugin marketplace remove flow-steward` if nothing else uses
it.

### Gemini CLI

Extract the release's `flow-steward-developer-<version>.tar.gz` into an empty
folder named `flow-steward-developer`; `gemini-extension.json` is at its root.
Then run `gemini extensions install /absolute/path/to/flow-steward-developer`,
`gemini extensions update flow-steward-developer` after replacing the folder with a
newer release, and `gemini extensions uninstall flow-steward-developer` to remove it.
Google replaced Gemini CLI with Antigravity CLI for unpaid and Google One
accounts; see [Gemini CLI extensions](https://geminicli.com/docs/extensions/reference/).

### Individual skills

You can instead copy a whole folder from `skills/` into the client's own skills
directory (`~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/`, or
the project equivalents). Do not install the same skill both ways.

## Check that it works

1. The client lists the four skills.
2. Ask, in a Flow Steward application checkout: "Which checks does the
   extension quality gate run?" The agent should answer from the checkout's
   `docs/standards/` and `lint.sh` rather than from memory.

Then, for example: "Create an extension that reads orders from our ERP",
"Publish version 1.2.0 of this extension to the catalog" or "Fix issue 123 and
open a pull request".

## Source

In the application repository this package lives in
`docs/agent-skills/flow-steward-developer`. Its manifests and icon are generated
from `docs/agent-skills/packages.json` and the product icon, and its
`skills/flow-steward-report-issue` is a copy of
`docs/agent-skills/shared/skills/flow-steward-report-issue`, which both
packages ship: change the source and run
`infra/tooling/agent-skills/sync_packages.py`, never the generated file. A unit
test fails when a generated file differs from its source. Release archives are
built from a committed revision with `infra/tooling/agent-skills/build_release.py`.
